sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Nepal Families Struggle for Death Certificates After China-Nepal Flood
cards.content: At the Pashupatinath temple, families are honoring loved ones who perished in the China-Nepal border flood, with many still missing. The government has ended rescue operations, and families are struggling to obtain death certificates, affecting compensation and inheritance. The law requires a 12-year waiting period before a missing person is presumed dead, with no provision for disasters like this flood. The legal hurdles come as Nepal faces a steep reconstruction bill, estimated at £3.6bn. The government is trying to find a solution, while the prime minister's office says it is "aware of the difficulties" the law may cause families.

cards.title: US Resident Arrested in Deadly School Shooting in British Columbia
cards.content: A 30-year-old US resident, James Cody Bryant, has been arrested in connection with a deadly school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, for allegedly encouraging the suspect, Jessie Van Rootselaar, 18. Bryant, charged with conspiracy to murder, had been in contact with Van Rootselaar, providing advice and technical support, and even agreed to livestream the attack. The shooting killed eight people, including six children, and Van Rootselaar died by self-inflicted gunshot. Bryant faces up to life in prison if found guilty. The shooting occurred at Van Rootselaar's home and at a secondary school in Tumbler Ridge.

cards.title: France sees widespread school protests, 1,015 injured
cards.content: Hundreds of thousands of people, including high-school pupils, parents, university students, and unions, protested across France, calling for better resources for schools and less police repression. Protesters marched from the Place de la République in Paris, with clashes reported in Lyon, Paris, and Marseille. According to the government, 215 students, 85 staff, and 715 police officers were injured. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, and Education Minister Édouard Geffray appealed for dialogue. The protests have been ongoing since mid-September, with students demanding better conditions in schools.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: US-led sanctions exhaust Iran's oil reserves, nuclear program remains intact
cards.content: The US-led blockade and sanctions against Iran have been effective, with Iran's remaining oil for sale nearly exhausted and crude production cut in half. Despite a dire economic situation, Iran shows no signs of folding, refusing to compromise on its nuclear program and negotiations on Strait of Hormuz transit. The regime has developed sophisticated networks to evade sanctions, and some analysts believe it may be receiving funds from unknown sources. The US has incurred significant costs in maintaining the blockade, and Iran may be waiting out the Trump administration, potentially outlasting the United States' willingness to stay the course.

cards.title: Stock futures stable; Strait of Hormuz crisis and AI wearables concerns weigh
cards.content: Stock futures are little changed following a mixed week on Wall Street, with oil tankers in the Middle East being hit in recent days as Iran refuses to budge on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, casting doubt on the global oil trade's recovery. Meanwhile, investors should be cautious of privacy concerns surrounding artificial intelligence-powered wearables, as major technology companies have bet on these devices to make their mark on the consumer hardware space.

cards.title: Microsoft CEO Prioritizes AI Deployment Within Enterprises
cards.content: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella emphasized the importance of "diffusion inside the enterprise" to adapt to the AI age, highlighting the need for AI tools to be widely deployed. Microsoft is trying to magnify its role in the AI boom, but faces challenges as Nvidia dominates in AI chips and Google's Gemini-powered services are popular. Nadella's AI strategy is centered around Copilot, but the company's sluggishness in keeping up with rapid changes has cost GitHub market share. Microsoft is now shifting to consumption-based pricing, with usage-based billing for Copilot Cowork, a new product. Nadella aims to empower nontechnical knowledge workers and has been downplaying the importance of world-beating models in isolation.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Northern Ireland's Thrombectomy Service Expands to 24/7 Operations
cards.content: Gemma O'Hara, a 40-year-old mother of three, suffered a brain stem stroke after returning from holiday, but was able to receive a thrombectomy procedure, which removed blood clots and restored blood flow to her brain. The procedure, a "miracle treatment," allowed her to recover well. Northern Ireland's regional thrombectomy service has expanded to operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, thanks to a £5m investment, allowing patients like Gemma to receive timely treatment. This increased availability has reduced the risk of death by almost 20% and increases a patient's chances of making a good recovery by more than 50%.

cards.title: Neck strain rises with screen time, experts warn
cards.content: The modern world can be challenging for necks, with millions spending hours with heads bent over laptops and smartphones. This can increase the load on necks by up to 60 pounds, leading to strain and discomfort. As we age, natural changes can cause neck problems, and technology's impact on posture adds to the strain. Neck pain can be mitigated through simple exercises, such as looking to the side and gently lengthening the neck. Good posture, regular movement, and breaks from screens can also help.

cards.title: Wales sees one-third of men die prematurely, urging health plan
cards.content: A report from men's charity Movember highlights alarming statistics on men's health in Wales, where a third of men die before their 75th birthday. Ben Lidgey's personal experience, which began with a minor testicular injury, led to a cancer diagnosis and later, mental health concerns. The report urges the Welsh government to develop a dedicated plan for men's health, citing high rates of premature mortality due to preventable conditions. The Welsh economy faces annual costs of £1.4 billion from the top five causes of male premature death. Experts emphasize the importance of addressing men's reluctance to seek help for both physical and mental health issues.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Coral restoration projects show promising signs of recovery
cards.content: Marine scientists are testing new methods to restore coral reefs damaged by warming oceans and other environmental pressures. Some projects are combining coral breeding with carefully selected resilient colonies to improve the chances of recovery.

cards.title: Underwater sensors reveal previously unknown whale migration patterns
cards.content: Networks of underwater microphones are helping scientists track whale movements across remote parts of the ocean. The recordings can reveal migration routes and important feeding areas without researchers having to follow the animals directly.

cards.title: Floating solar farms expand renewable energy production
cards.content: Floating solar installations are becoming an increasingly attractive option for regions where land is limited. Panels installed on reservoirs and other water bodies can generate electricity while reducing pressure on valuable land resources.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Global film festivals spotlight a new generation of filmmakers
cards.content: Film festivals around the world are giving greater attention to emerging directors and independent productions. Organisers say new filmmakers are experimenting with storytelling techniques and technologies while exploring social and cultural themes.

cards.title: New stadium technology changes how fans experience live sports
cards.content: Sports venues are adopting larger digital displays, real-time statistics and connected services to create more interactive experiences for spectators. The technology is also helping teams analyse matches and improve stadium operations.

cards.title: Music platforms experiment with new ways for artists to reach audiences
cards.content: Music platforms are experimenting with new discovery tools, personalised recommendations and direct connections between artists and listeners. The changes are reshaping how new musicians build audiences and release their work.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Global manufacturers increase investment in clean energy infrastructure
cards.content: Manufacturing companies are increasing spending on renewable electricity, energy-efficient equipment and cleaner production systems. Businesses are looking to reduce operating costs while preparing for stricter environmental requirements and changing energy markets.

cards.title: Global trade adjusts as companies rethink supply chains
cards.content: Companies are continuing to redesign supply chains in response to changing trade policies, transportation costs and geopolitical risks. Many businesses are looking for ways to diversify suppliers and make production networks more resilient.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
